messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The size of a “planet” can be measured in different ways—mass, radius, or even the extent of its atmosphere. In our own Solar System the biggest planet is **Jupiter**, with a mass about 318 times that of Earth and a radius roughly 11 times Earth's.

When we look beyond the Solar System, the record for the largest known planet (or planetary‑mass object) is held by **HD 100546 b**. This is a young, forming planet still embedded in the protoplanetary disk around the star HD 100546. Its radius is estimated to be about **2–3 times that of Jupiter** (roughly 20–30 % larger than the next‑largest exoplanets that have been confirmed). Because it is still accreting material, its exact size can change as it grows.

So:

| Context | Largest known object |
|---------|----------------------|
| Solar System | Jupiter (mass ≈ 318 M⊕, radius ≈ 11 R⊕) |
| Exoplanets (confirmed) | HD 100546 b (radius ≈ 2–3 R_Jup) |

If you’re interested in the most massive exoplanet, that title goes to **HD 100546 b** as well, with a mass estimated at several times that of Jupiter.
